moons.note: Moons with a name only, not those known by a provisional designation (S/2004 S 12) or a numeral alone (Jupiter LI). The moons of Orcus, Quaoar and Gonggong are kept, as those are often called dwarf planets.

sources.page: List of chemical element name etymologies

eponymous-elements.note: Elements whose "Nature of origin" is toponym, eponym, mythological or astrological, plus by hand cobalt and nickel (goblins), iridium (Iris), cadmium (Cadmus) and tellurium (the Earth).

sources.page: List of proper names of stars

star-names.note: Every name, those not approved by the IAU (marked †) included, plus the Sun by hand.

si-units.note: The 22 derived units with special names and the 7 base units.

sources.page: List of Nobel laureates in Physics
List of Nobel laureates in Chemistry

nobel-science.note: The laureate column links to redirects; each answer is the article the link leads to.

sources.page: List of missions to the Moon
List of missions to the Moon

space-probes.note: Merged by hand: crewed missions and craft that stayed in Earth orbit left out; landers, rovers and space telescopes beyond Earth orbit kept. The timeline's tables 1 to 8 are all read.

eponymous-diseases.note: Disease and syndrome articles only (not the people, signs or journals the page links to); diseases named after places or fictional characters left out; infections named after a person through their germ (brucellosis, salmonellosis) and a few common ones the page lacks (Ewing's sarcoma, Niemann–Pick disease) added by hand.

dinosaurs.note: Genus articles only: clades, periods, journals and people left out; an article titled with a binomial or "(dinosaur)" gives its genus.

viral-diseases.note: Rows whose infectious agent is a virus, and the diseases (not viruses) of the category.

sources.page: List of words ending in ology

ologies.note: All 25 tables, one per letter. Words that are not a field of study (apology, trilogy, tautology, anthology) left out.

gemstones.note: Gem minerals and varieties only, not mineral classes, rocks or people.

subatomic-particles.note: Observed particles only (the graviton left out), and named kinds of hadron rather than each excited state.

meter-scope.note: One-word names ending in -meter or -scope, plus medical and optical -scopes added by hand. The Chinese packs ask for instruments whose Chinese name ends in 计 or 镜 instead, built from the Chinese names of the same list.
